name: The Last Shift's Tokens
description: Nine brass shift-tokens on a loop of wire, each stamped with a man's number and scratched on the back with his name, green with forty years of calamine: the last shift of the Crown Drift, taken off the deep board. The ninth, the captain's, is rubbed bright from being counted.

name: The Drift-Captain's Last Entry
description: A torn leaf from the Crown Drift's day-book, in Abel Rowse's hand: the last shift's names, the hour they went down, and nothing after.

name: A Schedule of Heron Eggs
description: A Tallymen's printed schedule for a tax on herons' eggs taken at the dead tower above Sedgehithe, a farthing the egg, with the clerk's own column for eggs counted left blank and, under it in pencil, 'NOT ONE'.

name: The Barrow Register
description: The Struck Barrow's register: forty years of the Receiver's fair hand, a number a line, four thousand and eleven of them, and against each the date and the debt. No names. On the last page, in the same hand, a twelfth line nobody received.

name: The Copyists' List
description: A quire of names copied out of the Struck Barrow's register by the Quiet Hands' resurrection men, each priced for sale in the Undercroft with the dead man's age and trade.

name: Carrow's Speaking-Trumpet
description: A Sayer's speaking-trumpet of beaten brass as long as an arm, its bell engraved with the Circle's rings and, scratched over them, LOUDER. Blown into, it says nothing at all: whatever it carried, it carried only in her hands.

name: A Brass-Taker's Weigh-Slate
description: A roofing slate split for the purpose, chalked and wiped and chalked again by the brass-takers in the Crown Drift, the dust of a sleeve's worth of rubbing out still in its grain.

name: A Lead Debt-Weight's Tag
description: A tag of thin grey lead on a twist of wire, cut from one of the debt-weights in the Struck Barrow's weighing room, punched with a clerk's number and scratched over on the back with a pin.

name: The Receiver's Own Entry
description: A single leaf ruled as the Struck register is ruled, in a fair clerk's hand, its last line inked over and over until the nib went through and tore the paper beneath it.

name: The Creed of the Loud
description: A lecturer's sheet of good rag paper with five numbered lines on it, prised off the reeves' judging-bench at Holmwatch with the nail-hole still through its head and other hands' lines crowded under it.

name: The Dues-Roll of the Last Reeve
description: A short roll of water-stained vellum on a bone rod, the Lake-Reeves' dues as they were taken at Holmwatch's water-gate, kept by the last Reeve and hidden where the Tallymen's clerks never looked.
